newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ABB names Swiss country manager.
newsitem.headline: ABB names Swiss country manager.

text.p: Electrical engineering group ABB Asea Brown Boveri AG said it had appointed Alois Sonnenmoser, 57, as country manager for Switzerland, succeeding Edwin Somm, 63, who will step down on April 1.
Sonnenmoser, currently head of ABB Switzerland's Industrial and Building Systems Segment, will take over as president and chief executive officer of ABB Switzerland.
Felix Bagdasarjanz, chief executive of ABB Industrie AG, will succeed Sonnenmoser as responsible for the Industrial and Buildings Systems segment in ABB Switzerland.
Rolf Kehlhofer will also be joining the executive committee of ABB Switzerland and head the Power Generation segment.
Andreas Steiner, currently responsible for Power Generation, will assume responsibility for the Technology and Services Area, replacing Willi Roos, who will retire.

Somm, head of ABB Switzerland since the merger of Swedens's ASEA and Swiss BBC in 1988, told news conference he wanted to spend more time on his other jobs, which include the presidency of the Swiss Association of Machinery Manufacturers, the presidency of the Swiss Engineering Employers and board member at VORORT, the Swiss Federation of Commerce and Industry.

"I see great challenges in these associations," Somm said, noting Swiss industry is facing serious problems that have to be solved and he wanted to devote his time to the upcoming wage negotiations in the engineering industry this summer.
Somm, known in Switzerland for his outspoken views on the country's high costs, said there was a gap between most Swiss and its industry and he wanted to help bridge this gap.
Sonnenmoser, who Somm had recommended as his successor, joined BBC in 1964 as design engineer and then spent two years in Australia, negotiating a license agreement for BBC there.
After he returned to Switzerland, Sonnenmoser assumed increasingly important positions and was appointed member of the executive committee of ABB Switzerland in 1988.
Presenting himself to journalists, Sonnemoser said Somm had done an excellent job and he saw no reasons to dramatically change course.
He characterised himself as a believer in consensus decisions and the value of teamwork, although when necessary, he would also take decisions on his own.

Sonnenmoser said Switzerland's strengths as an industrial site were often overlooked and these included its educational system, the peaceful labour markets, workers willing to work, the fast movement of designs to finished products, a stable currency and low interest rates.
While he said that Switzerland must continue to deregulate and abolish cartels, he added that Swiss industry could do a lot on its own, such as simplify the management structures.
